summary: Sabine Klein-Schwind works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Harunaga Isaacson and was attested in 2026 as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg.

Sabine Löhr works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg, completing an M.A. and doctoral work under Lambert Schmithausen, and served as a Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft at Hamburg.
Sabriye Tenberken is a scholar in Tibetology. She studied at the University of Bonn from circa 1992 to 1997 and founded Braille Without Borders.
Sachin Kathale specializes in computational linguistics and Indology. He earned an M.Phil. from Jawaharlal Nehru University by 2007 and has served as a teacher at Samskrita Bharati.
Sachindra Kumar Maity was an Indian historian and Indologist. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham from circa 1953 to 1956 and held a post at Jadavpur University from circa 1958 to 1986.

Sadajiro Sugiura was an Indologist and philosopher. Educated at Rikkyo, the University of Pennsylvania, and Philadelphia Divinity School, he held posts at Pennsylvania, the Army War College, and Rikkyo University, where he became professor emeritus in 1931–1932.

Saerji works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has served on the faculty at Peking University, where he was an associate professor attested between 2010 and 2016, and remained on the faculty as attested in 2026.
Sai Susarla works in computational Indology. He was dean at MIT World Peace University in 2019 and held a post at the Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation in 2025.

Said Reza Huseini specializes in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at King's College London, Jawaharlal Nehru University (circa 2010–2012), and Leiden University (circa 2017–2021).

Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi studied at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University and under Mohammad Habib. He worked in Indology and history, holding posts at Jammu and Kashmir, SOAS, JNU, AMU, and the Australian National University (1967–1986).
Sakda Hemthep is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.Phil. at Cardiff University under Max Deeg and Peter Harvey by 2014. As of 2026, he is a PhD researcher at Ghent University.

Sakkottai Krishnaswami Aiyangar was an Indologist and historian educated at the University of Madras. He lectured at Central College, Bangalore (1899–1909), held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at Madras (1914–1929), and edited the Journal of Indian History.
Sakunoshin Motoda was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kenyon College, Columbia University, and the University of Pennsylvania. He held a post at Rikkyo University from circa 1899 to 1923.
Sakutaro Fujioka was a scholar of Japanology and history. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1894 to 1897 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1900 to 1910.

Sakya Trizin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Appey Rinpoche and Tritsho Khenpo Rinchen, and has taught numerous students, including Steven Weinberger and Sam van Schaik.

Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and several traditional masters, founded Sakya Centre, Sakya College, and Sakya Institute, and served as Abbot of Sakya Monastery until 2017.

Sakyong Mipham Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Penor Rinpoche; he succeeded Chögyam Trungpa and served on Naropa University's board until 2018.

Sallie B. King specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz and served at James Madison University as professor (circa 1992–2008) and professor emerita (circa 2008–2017).
Sally J. Sutherland Goldman is an Indologist who completed her PhD at UC Berkeley in 1979 under Shivram Dattatray Joshi. She taught at UC Berkeley, where she is Senior Lecturer Emerita.
Sally McAra specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000), where she was supervised by Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.
